claim: Dragon's Back is an intermediate ~8.5km, ~4-hour ridge hike from Shek O Peak to Big Wave Bay with ocean and island views.
quote: The difficulty is Intermediate, with approximately 8.5 km distance and 4 hours duration. The route goes from Shek O Peninsula Viewing Point > Shek O Peak > Dragon's Back & Pottinger Gap > Big Wave Bay.

claim: Lion Rock is a steep 6.5km one-way hike with 436m elevation gain, most popularly started near Wong Tai Sin MTR.
quote: The distance is 6.5km one-way track with 436m elevation gain and very steep start and mid section to the peak... The most popular starting point is Wong Tai Sin because it's well-connected by public transport including the MTR.

claim: The Victoria Peak loop along Lugard and Harlech Roads is a mostly flat paved walk with harbour views, reachable by the Peak Tram.
quote: The well-marked loop offers a mostly flat walk with uninterrupted views over Victoria Harbour, Central and Kowloon. The route follows Lugard Road and Harlech Road... You can start near the Peak Tower or Peak Galleria; both are easy to reach by public transport, including the historic Peak Tram.

claim: Ferries leave Central Pier 4 for Lamma (25-40 min, HKD17-25), Pier 5 for Cheung Chau (35-55 min), and Pier 6 for Mui Wo/Lantau (50-60 min); no booking needed, pay by Octopus.
quote: Lamma Island (Pier 4) Journey time: 25-40 minutes... Cheung Chau (Pier 5) Journey time: 35-55 minutes... Mui Wo/Lantau (Pier 6) Journey time: 50-60 minutes... No advance booking required; just turn up and pay at the pier

claim: The Lamma Island Family Trail is an easy ~5km flat concreted hour-long walk linking Yung Shue Wan and Sok Kwu Wan, ending at the seafood restaurants of Sok Kwu Wan.
quote: The Lamma Island Family Trail is a very easy hike/walk of about 5km across Lamma Island, connecting the two ferry piers... no steep inclines, no steps and the path is all concreted... that takes around an hour.

claim: Tai O is a Lantau stilt-house fishing village ('Venice of Hong Kong') reached via MTR to Tung Chung then bus 11 (~1 hour), often combined with the Big Buddha via Ngong Ping cable car and bus 21.
quote: Start by taking the MTR Tung Chung Line to Tung Chung Station (about 35 minutes). From there... take Bus 11 to Tai O, which takes around an hour... take the 360 Ngong Ping Cable Car... After spending some time seeing the Big Buddha and Ngong Ping village, get bus 21 to Tai O

claim: Repulse Bay is reached by bus 6/6x/260 from Central's Exchange Square; Shek O and Big Wave Bay are reached by bus 9 from Shau Kei Wan MTR Exit A3.
quote: From Central, take bus 6, 6x or 260 from Exchange Square... to the Repulse Bay Beach bus stop... From Shau Kei Wan Bus Terminus (adjacent to MTR Shau Kei Wan Station Exit A3), take bus 9 and alight at the Shek O Beach stop.

claim: Big Wave Bay, reached via bus 9 toward Shek O, is known for surfable waves rolling in from the Tathong Channel.
quote: Big Wave Bay Beach is best known for its large waves that roll in from the Tathong Channel.

claim: June in Hong Kong is hot, humid (often >80%) and the wettest month (~450-500mm rain); hiking is best done early morning and visitors risk heatstroke.
quote: June in Hong Kong is hot, humid, and rainy, with temperatures hovering around 28-31C... humidity often above 80%... June is typically Hong Kong's wettest month... For hiking trails, it's recommended to hike early in the morning.

claim: June falls in typhoon season; if Typhoon Signal No. 8 is issued, transport and shops shut down, so visitors should check the Hong Kong Observatory daily.
quote: Always check the Hong Kong Observatory website for daily forecasts and warnings, as if a Typhoon Signal No. 8 is issued, most of the city, including shops and public transport, will shut down.
